title: Fearlessness first
hook: Krishna's list of divine qualities starts with fearlessness, for an Arjuna who dropped his bow
carry: fearlessness is the first divine quality

segments.voice: Yesterday, purushottama: the perishable, the imperishable, and the highest person beyond both. Today, a list that starts somewhere unexpected.

Go back to where the Gita began. Arjuna stands in his chariot between two armies and sees his teachers, cousins and uncles on the other side. His limbs give way, his mouth goes dry, his great bow Gandiva slips from his hand, and he sinks down, overcome with grief. Fifteen chapters later, Krishna gives him a list: the qualities of someone born to a divine inheritance. And the very first word, before truth, before compassion, is abhaya. Fearlessness. Why?
screen: `ARJUNA DROPS HIS BOW.` → `FIFTEEN CHAPTERS LATER, A LIST.` → `THE FIRST WORD: FEARLESSNESS.`

segments.voice: Verses one to three are one long sentence. Fearlessness. Purity of heart. Steadiness in knowledge and practice. Giving. Self-control. Sacrifice. Study of scripture. Discipline. Straightness. Then: doing no harm, truth, freedom from anger, letting go, peace, not gossiping about others, kindness to all beings, not being greedy, gentleness, modesty, not being fickle. And to close: energy, forgiveness, endurance, cleanliness, no malice, no excess pride. Twenty-six in all. Krishna calls them daivi sampad, the divine inheritance, like a fortune you're born into. Why fearlessness first? The text doesn't say. One answer teachers give: without it, the others don't hold. It's hard to tell the truth if you're afraid, hard to forgive, to give, to stay gentle. Fear quietly bends everything else. The second word, sattva-samshuddhi, purity of heart, is about what's underneath: clean motives, not only clean hands. Together they make today's line. Verse four gives the opposite list, briefly: hypocrisy, arrogance, too much pride, anger, harshness and ignorance. Tomorrow, that side. Verse five: the divine inheritance leads to freedom, the other to bondage. Then Krishna turns to Arjuna, who began this whole conversation overcome with grief, and says something gentle: do not grieve, Arjuna. You were born to the divine inheritance. The inheritance is already his. That's the teaching: in Hinduism, fearlessness isn't toughness. It grows from knowing who you are, the self that, as chapter two said, no weapon can cut. It's why so many images of the gods show one palm raised toward you: abhaya mudra, the gesture that says, do not fear.
screen: `TWENTY-SIX QUALITIES.` · `FEARLESSNESS FIRST.` · `PURITY OF HEART UNDERNEATH.` · `DON'T GRIEVE. IT'S ALREADY HIS.` · `ABHAYA MUDRA: DO NOT FEAR.` · then, large: `FEARLESSNESS FIRST.`

segments.voice: Picture an image of a Hindu god with the right palm raised toward you, abhaya mudra: do not fear. Then find one small fear you're carrying, a conversation you're avoiding, and hold it in front of that open hand. Breathe in and feel where it sits; breathe out and let it soften. If you pray, ask for courage; if you don't, ask quietly: if this fear were smaller, what would I do?
Abhaya, fearlessness, no fear. Gita sixteen, one to five: the first of twenty-six qualities of the divine inheritance, daivi sampad, alongside purity of heart.
Your line: fearlessness is the first divine quality. Courage first, a clean heart underneath. Day two hundred thirteen, in the books.

howItsDone: Some Hindu teachers use Gita 16.1–16.3 as a list of virtues to cultivate, opening with abhaya (fearlessness); many murtis and images of the gods show abhaya mudra, the raised open palm that says 'do not fear'.

chat.says: ok so i signed up to explain diwali to my whole history class friday and now i'm SCARED 😭 nani just held up her palm and said 'abhaya.' what does that mean
options: fearlessness, the first divine quality in the gita. krishna said it to arjuna after he dropped his bow.
it means never feel fear at all. if you're scared, you're doing it wrong.
it's a warrior thing, only for people going into battle.
chat.meaning: Gita 16 opens its list of divine qualities with abhaya, fearlessness, and Krishna tells Arjuna, who had sunk down in grief, that he was born to that inheritance. The raised palm, abhaya mudra, says the same: do not fear.

tie.story: Arjuna dropped his bow in grief, and Krishna later told him fearlessness is the first divine quality and that he was born to it.
tie.friend: Priya can stand up and talk about Diwali knowing courage is part of her own inheritance, not something to fake.
tie.you: what fear would you hold up to that raised palm?

daivi sampad.meaning: the divine inheritance: the good qualities you're born into

sattva-samshuddhi.meaning: purity of heart: clean motives underneath

Arjuna.meaning: the warrior prince Krishna teaches in the Gita

abhaya mudra.meaning: the raised open palm of the gods: 'do not fear'
